title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: NADINE'S NOTES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Nadine Tran, a forty-three-year-old payroll clerk in Olympia, Washington.
For nineteen years, every county paycheck went out on time. Nobody ever said thanks.
So Nadine started a very quiet war.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE WRONG LIST
segments.quote: The hardest arithmetic to master is that which enables us to count our blessings.
segments.author: Eric Hoffer
lines: On her birthday, she ate a gas station cupcake and listed everything wrong with her life.
Her mom read her a line off the fridge, from Eric Hoffer, a dock worker who wrote books:
The hardest arithmetic to master is that which enables us to count our blessings.
She flipped the list and started counting.
Number one: old Mr. Hale, who hired her at his hardware store at sixteen.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE DRAWER
segments.quote: Feeling gratitude and not expressing it is like wrapping a present and not giving it.
segments.author: William Arthur Ward
lines: She wrote Mr. Hale a note. It sat in her drawer for three weeks.
Her coworker Lou quoted the writer William Arthur Ward:
Feeling gratitude and not expressing it is like wrapping a present and not giving it.
Nadine bought a stamp at lunch and mailed it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE VOICEMAIL
segments.quote: At times our own light goes out and is rekindled by a spark from another person.
segments.author: Albert Schweitzer
lines: Two weeks later, a voicemail. Mr. Hale was eighty-eight. Her note was on his fridge.
She cried in her car.
He'd mailed her a line from the doctor Albert Schweitzer:
At times our own light goes out and is rekindled by a spark from another person.
So she made a rule. One note, every Friday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SQUEAKY CHAIR
segments.quote: I think I have learned that the best way to lift one's self up is to help some one else.
segments.author: Booker T. Washington
lines: Next came Ray, the night janitor. Nine years of emptying her trash.
She felt silly. Then she remembered Booker T. Washington:
I think I have learned that the best way to lift one's self up is to help some one else.
She left the note on the bin. Monday, her squeaky chair stopped squeaking.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE DEPUTY
segments.author: Aesop
lines: Then Deputy Walsh, who yelled about overtime every month. Nadine typed a nasty email.
Lou slid over his coffee mug, with a line from Aesop's fables:
Kindness effects more than severity.
She deleted it and wrote, Thanks for catching that error in March.
Walsh brought donuts. He still yells.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE ENVELOPE
segments.quote: I would maintain that thanks are the highest form of thought, and that gratitude is happiness doubled by wonder.
segments.author: G. K. Chesterton
lines: Soon there were sticky notes all over the county building.
On her next birthday, a fat envelope. Two hundred notes.
On top, Lou had copied the English writer G. K. Chesterton:
I would maintain that thanks are the highest form of thought, and that gratitude is happiness doubled by wonder.
Nadine counted them twice. It's what she does.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Count your blessings. Mail the note. Pass the spark. Lift someone. Be kind. Say thanks.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Count what you've got. Mail the note. Pass the spark. Lift someone up. Skip the nasty email. Say thanks.
I sent my barber a thank-you note once. He wrote back, For what?
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
